papers.title: Multiple Adaptive Bayesian Linear Regression for Scalable Bayesian Optimization with Warm Start
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) is a model-based approach for gradient-free black-box function optimization. Typically, BO is powered by a Gaussian process (GP), whose algorithmic complexity is cubic in the number of evaluations. Hence, GP-based BO cannot leverage large amounts of past or related function evaluations, for example, to warm start the BO procedure. We develop a multiple adaptive Bayesian linear regression model as a scalable alternative whose complexity is linear in the number of observations. The multiple Bayesian linear regression models are coupled through a shared feedforward neural network, which learns a joint representation and transfers knowledge across machine learning problems.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该方法可扩展贝叶斯优化到大规模历史数据，但未涉及约束处理、不确定性量化或在生物力学设计中的应用。
llm.why_not_core: No constraint handling, no explicit uncertainty quantification beyond standard BO, and no demonstration on biomechanics or implant design problems.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决高斯过程贝叶斯优化计算复杂度高、难以利用大量历史数据的问题。
summary_zh.method: 提出多自适应贝叶斯线性回归模型，通过共享神经网络耦合多个模型实现迁移学习。
summary_zh.result: 模型复杂度与观测数线性相关，能利用相关函数评估加速优化。
summary_zh.validation: 在标准基准优化函数上测试，与GP-BO比较性能。

summary_en.motivation: To scale Bayesian optimization to large datasets by replacing the cubic-complexity Gaussian process with a linear-complexity model that can leverage past evaluations.
summary_en.method: Proposes multiple adaptive Bayesian linear regression models coupled through a shared feedforward neural network for transfer learning across optimization tasks.
summary_en.result: The approach achieves linear time complexity in the number of observations and effectively transfers knowledge to warm-start optimization.
summary_en.validation: Validated on synthetic benchmark optimization functions, demonstrating competitive performance with standard GP-based BO.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究选区激光熔化过程中的温度与残余应力场建模，未涉及生物医用植入物中的多孔结构、应力屏蔽或疲劳性能。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on thermal and residual stress modeling of SLM process without any link to porous structures, stress shielding, stiffness matching, fatigue testing, or osseointegration for biomedical implants.

summary_zh.motivation: 理解SLM过程的温度与残余应力分布
summary_zh.method: 采用有限元热-力耦合模型模拟
summary_zh.result: 预测了温度场和残余应力场分布
summary_zh.validation: 与文献或实验数据对比验证

summary_en.motivation: To understand temperature and residual stress evolution in selective laser melting for process optimization.
summary_en.method: A finite element thermal-mechanical coupled model was developed to simulate the SLM process.
summary_en.result: Temperature fields and residual stress distributions were predicted, showing high stresses near the melt pool.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed by comparing simulated temperature profiles and residual stress magnitudes with literature data.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the processability of pure copper via selective laser melting.

summary_en.result: Nearly fully dense copper parts were obtained.

summary_en.motivation: To develop NiTi shape memory alloys with both high damping capacity and Elinvar effect.
summary_en.method: Layer-structured NiTi alloys were fabricated via selective laser melting (SLM).
summary_en.result: The as-built NiTi exhibited high damping properties and an Elinvar effect over a wide temperature range.
summary_en.validation: Damping and elastic modulus were characterized through dynamic mechanical analysis.

summary_en.motivation: To develop a macroscopic thermal finite element model for predicting temperature distributions during selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: A thermal finite element model is built at the macroscopic scale to simulate heat transfer in the powder bed process.
summary_en.result: The model captures the influence of process parameters on thermal histories and melt pool dimensions.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed by comparing simulation results with experimental temperature measurements and published data.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of microstructure anisotropy on the mechanical properties of reduced activation ferritic/martensitic steel fabricated by selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Samples were fabricated via selective laser melting and characterized for microstructure and mechanical properties through tensile testing and microscopy.
summary_en.result: Significant anisotropy in microstructure was correlated with directional variations in mechanical properties.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical properties were validated through tensile tests and microstructural analysis.
